scan_focus: Official agent frameworks, GPU tools, ML frameworks, MCP ecosystem, hot trending repos

agent_frameworks.name: anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python
agent_frameworks.description: Official Anthropic Claude Agent SDK for Python. Powers orchestration of Claude Code subagents programmatically.
march_2026_highlights: v0.1.49 (Mar 20): AgentDefinition gains 'skills', 'memory', 'mcpServers' fields — agents now declare their full capability set declaratively
v0.1.49: session tagging (tag_session()), renaming (rename_session()), typed RateLimitEvent
v0.1.49: per-turn usage preserved on AssistantMessage — enables token-cost accounting per agent turn
v0.1.50 (Mar 20): get_session_info() function + 'tag'/'created_at' on SDKSessionInfo
v0.1.50: bundled Claude CLI bumped to 2.1.81
Claude Code 2.1.76: MCP elicitation — MCP servers can now show interactive forms/dialogs mid-task
Claude Code 2.1.77: Opus 4.6 output token limit raised to 64k, context cap 128k, session resume 45% faster
Claude Code 2.1.78: StopFailure hook + persistent plugin data storage
Claude Code 2.1.79: Console auth flag, startup memory -18MB
Claude Code 2.1.80: rate limit visibility in statusline, parallel tool result handling fixed in session resumption
Claude Code 2.1.81: bare mode for scripted -p calls, channel-based permission relays, multi-session re-auth fixed
Hooks (12 events): agent_id + agent_type fields added for subagent tracking
Hooks: StopFailure event fires when agent hits a terminal error — use for auto-recovery
agent_frameworks.nba_relevance: HIGH — our 4h Brain trigger uses Claude Agent SDK to spawn research/feature/evolution subagents. AgentDefinition.skills + memory fields enable declaring skill sets declaratively. session tagging enables per-experiment tracking.
agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: Use tag_session() to label each 4h Brain cycle with generation number + best Brier score. Use AgentDefinition with 'skills' field to declare our 4 specialized agent team capabilities. Use StopFailure hook to auto-restart failed evolution islands.

agent_frameworks.name: google/adk-python
agent_frameworks.description: Google Agent Development Kit: open-source, code-first Python toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying sophisticated AI agents. Model-agnostic, supports A2A protocol natively.
march_2026_highlights: v1.27.3 (Mar 23): protection for arbitrary module imports — security hardening
v2.0.0a1 pre-release (Mar 18): workflow runtime with graph-based execution engine — sequential, fan-out/fan-in, loops
Native A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol support — agents on Agent Engine can discover/talk to agents on other platforms
Agent Engine on Vertex AI now supports A2A Protocol — cross-org agent communication
Gemini 3 Pro/Flash (Mar 2026): reasoning control, stateful tool use via Thought Signatures, computer use
ADK release cadence: roughly bi-weekly (very active)
agent_frameworks.nba_relevance: MEDIUM — if we ever want to run Gemini 3 Flash as a research subagent (free API tier) alongside Claude. A2A protocol could allow our HF Spaces to register as agents and report status back to Brain.
agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: Gemini 3 Flash has a free API tier with 1M context. Use as a secondary research agent in Karpathy loop for cost reduction. ADK's graph-based workflow runtime (v2.0.0a1) is a clean pattern for our 4-step Karpathy cycle.

agent_frameworks.name: openai/openai-agents-python
agent_frameworks.description: Lightweight, powerful framework for multi-agent workflows. Production successor to Swarm. Provider-agnostic, supports 100+ LLMs via litellm.
march_2026_highlights: v0.13.0 (Mar 23): tool search tool with namespace support, gpt-5.4 mini for computer use
Provider-agnostic: supports 100+ LLMs beyond OpenAI models
GPT-5.4 mini now available in Codex for lighter coding tasks — 2x faster than GPT-5 mini
Voice agents via gpt-realtime-1.5 model
Session management: automatic conversation history tracking across runs
Codex: app-server TUI updates, ChatGPT device-code sign-in, new user prompt hook
agent_frameworks.nba_relevance: LOW — we use Claude exclusively. But the provider-agnostic pattern + guardrails API are worth studying for our agent architecture.
agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: Guardrails pattern: input/output validation on every agent turn. Apply to our feature_engineer agent so it validates feature category exists in engine.py before proposing. Also: handoff pattern for clean agent delegation.

agent_frameworks.name: microsoft/agent-framework
agent_frameworks.description: Microsoft Agent Framework: unified convergence of AutoGen + Semantic Kernel. Graph-based workflows, multi-provider LLM support, A2A + MCP interoperability. RC5 as of Mar 20.
march_2026_highlights: RC5 (Mar 20): API surface now stable, GA expected end of March 2026
AutoGen entering maintenance mode — focus shifting entirely to Microsoft Agent Framework
Graph-based workflows: sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat patterns with streaming + checkpointing
DevUI: interactive developer interface for testing/debugging agent workflows
OpenTelemetry integration built-in for distributed tracing
A2A + MCP interoperability standard — works with Google ADK, Anthropic Claude
AF Labs: experimental packages for benchmarking, RL, and research
agent_frameworks.nba_relevance: LOW — we use Claude Code subagents. But AF Labs benchmarking package and the RL (reinforcement learning) extension are worth watching for future meta-learning of evolution hyperparameters.
agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: AF Labs RL extension pattern for hyperparameter optimization via reinforcement learning. Their group chat + checkpointing pattern is cleaner than our current sequential 4-agent Karpathy loop.

agent_frameworks.name: langchain-ai/langgraph
agent_frameworks.description: Graph-based agent orchestration framework. Most production-hardened option with checkpointing, time-travel debugging, durable execution. 34.5M monthly downloads.
march_2026_highlights: LangGraph 1.0 now generally available
Type-safe streaming (version='v2'): unified StreamPart output with type, ns, data keys on every chunk
Type-safe invoke (version='v2'): GraphOutput object with .value and .interrupts attributes
Pydantic/dataclass coercion: invoke() output auto-coerced to declared types
Fixed time travel with interrupts and subgraphs
Deep Agents v0.5.0 (Mar 24): async subagents — non-blocking background tasks
Used in production by Klarna, Uber, LinkedIn
agent_frameworks.nba_relevance: MEDIUM — our Karpathy loop is effectively a LangGraph-style DAG running inside Claude Code. Deep Agents v0.5.0 async subagents pattern is relevant for parallelizing our 4 research subagents.
agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: Deep Agents v0.5.0 async subagent pattern: spawn all 4 Karpathy subagents (repo-scout, market-analyst, feature-engineer, evolution-optimizer) in parallel rather than sequentially. Estimated time savings: 3x speedup per Brain cycle.

agent_frameworks.name: crewAIInc/crewAI
agent_frameworks.description: Framework for orchestrating role-playing, autonomous AI agents. Collaborative intelligence for complex tasks.
march_2026_highlights: Better memory: vector database integration for cross-session agent memory
Improved parallel processing: independent tasks execute simultaneously by default
NOTE: our MEMORY.md says CrewAI is dead/replaced by Claude Code subagents — do NOT re-introduce

agent_frameworks.what_to_steal: Nothing. We use Claude Code subagents exclusively per user decision 2026-03-24.

~12,500 tokens/sec on H100 80GB at FP8 for Llama 3.3 70B

gpu_and_training_tools.name: microsoft/BitNet

march_2026_highlights: 35.4k stars as of March 18 week
370 HN points — strong developer interest in CPU-only inference
1-bit quantization allows running large models on CPU/laptop
gpu_and_training_tools.nba_relevance: LOW for training. MEDIUM for VM — if we ever need a local LLM on our 969MB VM for feature proposal generation, BitNet-quantized models could fit. Currently we use Claude API so irrelevant.
gpu_and_training_tools.what_to_steal: Nothing immediately. File under: if we ever lose Claude API access, BitNet + Qwen3-1.7B could run feature proposals on VM.

gpu_and_training_tools.name: NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B
gpu_and_training_tools.description: NVIDIA agentic model. Hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE. 1M token context. Built for agentic, reasoning, tool-use, chat. 4x faster than Nemotron Nano 2.
march_2026_highlights: Released March 2026 on HuggingFace
30B total params, 3B active (MoE) — efficient inference
52 layers: 23 MoE + 23 Mamba-2 + 6 GQA layers
1M token context window — ideal for long-horizon agentic workflows
3.3x higher throughput than Qwen3-30B on H200
Reasoning ON/OFF modes + configurable thinking budget
FP8 + NVFP4 quantized checkpoints available on HF (released 2026/03/11)
NVIDIA NeMo Agent Toolkit: framework-agnostic library to connect agent components
gpu_and_training_tools.nba_relevance: MEDIUM — if run on Google Colab (T4 GPU), Nemotron-Nano-4B variant could serve as a local feature-engineering LLM. The 30B variant needs H200.
gpu_and_training_tools.what_to_steal: Nemotron-3-Nano-4B (not 30B) — check if it fits in Colab T4 (16GB) for use as a local feature-proposal LLM. The reasoning budget control is useful: low budget for fast feature screening, high budget for novel feature design.

gpu_and_training_tools.name: lightpanda-io/browser

gpu_and_training_tools.what_to_steal: Nothing immediately. Watch for if we add web scraping to our data pipeline.

gpu_and_training_tools.description: Current free GPU options state as of March 2026

hot_trending_repos.name: obra/superpowers
hot_trending_repos.description: Agentic skills framework and software development methodology for coding agents. Composable 'skills' + structured workflow: spec -> plan -> TDD implementation. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, and 5+ others.
march_2026_highlights: 95k stars as of March 18 week, +37.8k stars in March alone — fastest growing agent framework
Works with Claude Code natively
Spec-first approach: forces the agent to produce a spec you approve before coding
TDD enforcement: red/green tests written first
Compatible with our .claude/agents/ skill structure
hot_trending_repos.nba_relevance: MEDIUM — their skill composition pattern is directly relevant to our Claude Code skill system (/karpathy-loop, /tony-bloom, /progress-10pct). Could formalize our feature-engineer workflow.
hot_trending_repos.what_to_steal: The spec-first + implementation plan pattern for our feature-engineer agent. Before proposing a new feature category, the agent produces: (1) spec of what the feature measures, (2) implementation plan, (3) expected Brier delta. Prevents half-baked feature proposals.

hot_trending_repos.name: vectorize-io/hindsight
hot_trending_repos.description: Agent Memory That Learns. Treat memory as first-class substrate for reasoning. Core ops: retain, recall, reflect + mental models that auto-update. SOTA on LongMemEval benchmark. MCP server available.
march_2026_highlights: Trending on GitHub since March 15, 2026
MCP server mode: add persistent memory to any MCP-compatible agent in 2 lines
LLM Wrapper: add memory to existing agent with 2 lines of code
SOTA on LongMemEval benchmark
Three core ops: retain (store), recall (search), reflect (reason)
Mental models auto-update as memories accumulate
Built on vectorize.io vector DB
hot_trending_repos.nba_relevance: MEDIUM — our Brain agent currently has no persistent memory between 4h cycles beyond git commits. Hindsight MCP server could give Brain agent persistent memory of experiment outcomes, allowing it to reason about 100+ generations of evolution history.
hot_trending_repos.what_to_steal: Add Hindsight MCP server to Brain's Claude Code config. Use 'retain' to store every experiment outcome (brier, model_type, feature_count, generation). Use 'reflect' to ask 'what feature categories improved Brier the most in last 50 generations?' before making config decisions.

hot_trending_repos.name: autogluon/tabarena
hot_trending_repos.description: Living benchmark for ML on tabular data. 25M trained models cached. 16 models evaluated: GBDTs, neural nets, foundation models (TabPFNv2, TabICL, TabDPT).
march_2026_highlights: TabArena-v0.1 public with 16 models
Key finding: diverse ensemble (GBDT + DL) beats GBDT-only ensemble
TabPFNv2 significantly outperforms others on datasets <=10k samples, <=500 features
Neural networks strongest single models AFTER post-hoc ensembling
TabICL strong in-context learning for small-data regimes
TabPFN-2.5: scales to 50k samples (5x TabPFNv2), 2000 features (4x), matches AutoGluon 4h ensemble in single forward pass
TabICL v2 (2026): faster + better than v1
hot_trending_repos.nba_relevance: HIGH — this validates our GBDT stack AND reveals we should add TabPFNv2 or TabICLv2 as a stacking meta-learner. Our 6135 features exceed TabPFN-2.5's 2000 feature limit — we'd need to pass evolved feature subsets (e.g., top 63 from S10).
hot_trending_repos.what_to_steal: Use TabPFN-2.5 or TabICLv2 on the evolved 63-feature subset from S10. Add as an additional base model in stacking ensemble. Expected: -0.003 to -0.005 Brier on small validation folds. Distillation engine: convert TabPFN-2.5 -> compact tree ensemble for HF Space deployment.

papers_and_benchmarks.what_to_steal: Add TabICLv2 as stacking base model using evolved 63-feature subset. Run on Colab T4. Feed predict_proba() output as meta-features to our final XGBoost blender. TabArena shows this adds 0.5-1.5% over GBDT-only ensemble.

papers_and_benchmarks.name: TabPFN-2.5 Model Report
papers_and_benchmarks.description: Next-gen tabular foundation model. Scales to 50k samples, 2000 features. Matches AutoGluon 4h ensemble in single forward pass. Distillation engine available.
papers_and_benchmarks.what_to_steal: Use TabPFN-2.5 distillation: train TabPFN-2.5 on our dataset, distill to compact tree ensemble, deploy on HF Spaces CPU. This converts the foundation model's knowledge into a deployable artifact without GPU requirement.

papers_and_benchmarks.name: State of Tabular Foundation Models (2026)
papers_and_benchmarks.description: Survey of TabPFN-2.5, TabICLv2, TabDPT performance across regimes. Key: foundation models win on small data, GBDTs win on large data.
papers_and_benchmarks.what_to_steal: For our 3000-5000 game training window: we're in TabPFN territory (could gain from foundation models). For our 6000+ feature engine: must use feature selection first to get under 2000 features before TabPFN. Our GA already selects ~63 features — pipe that subset directly to TabPFN-2.5.

top_5_actionable.name: TabICLv2 as stacking meta-learner
top_5_actionable.action: On Colab T4: pip install tabicl, run TabICLv2.fit(X_train_63feat, y_train), add predict_proba() output as 2 meta-features to XGBoost final blender. The 63-feature evolved subset from S10 is already within TabICLv2's regime. Run as post-hoc addition to existing best model.
top_5_actionable.nba_fit: TabArena shows GBDT+foundation model ensemble outperforms GBDT-only. Our current Brier 0.21867 could drop to ~0.21467 with proper stacking.
top_5_actionable.constraint: Run on Colab T4 only, not VM

top_5_actionable.name: Parallel Karpathy subagents
top_5_actionable.action: Install claude-code-workflow-orchestration plugin. Modify .claude/skills/karpathy-loop to dispatch all 4 subagents (repo-scout, market-analyst, feature-engineer, evolution-optimizer) in parallel using task decomposition. Merge results before decision step.
top_5_actionable.nba_fit: Not directly a Brier improvement but 3x Brain cycle speedup means more research iterations per day. Indirect improvement via faster research velocity.
top_5_actionable.constraint: Test with --dry-run before deploying to 4h cron

top_5_actionable.name: Hindsight MCP persistent Brain memory
top_5_actionable.action: Add Hindsight MCP server to Brain's Claude Code ~/.claude.json mcpServers config. After each 4h cycle: retain(experiment_id, brier, model_type, feature_count, top_features, generation). Before each decision: recall('feature categories that improved Brier') + reflect('what config changes correlate with Brier improvements'). Enables data-driven Brain decisions across hundreds of generations.
top_5_actionable.nba_fit: Currently Brain makes config decisions without systematic memory of what worked. Hindsight gives it 200+ generation history to reason over.
top_5_actionable.constraint: Hindsight uses vectorize.io vector DB — check if free tier sufficient for our volume

top_5_actionable.name: Session tagging for experiment tracking
top_5_actionable.action: In autonomous-cycle.sh: after each Brain run, call claude_sdk.tag_session(f'gen{generation}_brier{best_brier:.5f}'). Use get_session_info() to retrieve session metadata for correlation analysis. This creates a searchable audit trail linking Brain decisions to evolution outcomes.
top_5_actionable.nba_fit: Operational improvement: enables debugging 'which Brain decisions preceded Brier improvements'.

top_5_actionable.name: TabPFN-2.5 distillation to tree ensemble
top_5_actionable.action: On Colab T4: (1) pip install tabpfn==2.5, (2) fit TabPFN-2.5 on our dataset using top 63 evolved features, (3) use TabPFN-2.5's built-in distillation engine to export as compact tree ensemble, (4) deploy distilled model to HF Spaces (CPU-compatible). This gives us foundation model quality at tree-based inference speed.
top_5_actionable.nba_fit: TabPFN-2.5 matches AutoGluon 4h ensembles in a single forward pass. Distilled version should preserve most of this gain while running on HF Spaces CPU.
top_5_actionable.constraint: Must use top 63 features (not all 6135) due to TabPFN 2000-feature limit. Distilled model must be serialized and pushed to HF Space.

key_ecosystem_insights.agent_framework_winner_2026: Claude Code + subagents has become the dominant agentic coding paradigm (95k stars for obra/superpowers which is Claude Code-first). OpenAI Agents SDK (20.3k) and Google ADK (18.6k) are strong but Claude Code ecosystem is the most active.
key_ecosystem_insights.mcp_maturity: 1,864+ MCP servers indexed. Top categories: browser automation (Playwright-MCP), memory (Hindsight, Context7), structured thinking. MCP is now the universal agent integration layer.
key_ecosystem_insights.tabular_ml_2026_verdict: GBDTs remain the best individual models for large tabular data. TabPFN-2.5 and TabICLv2 beat GBDTs on small data (<50k samples). Our GA should evolve blend weights across {XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, extra_trees, TabICLv2} — not just select from 4 GBDT types.
key_ecosystem_insights.parallel_agents: Async/parallel subagent patterns now mature (Deep Agents v0.5.0, claude-code-workflow-orchestration). Sequential 4-agent loops are obsolete — all major frameworks now support parallel dispatch.
key_ecosystem_insights.memory_systems: Hindsight (vectorize-io) is SOTA on LongMemEval. Context7 dominates FastMCP memory category. doobidoo/mcp-memory-service has autonomous consolidation. All three are MCP-native.
key_ecosystem_insights.gpu_options_2026: Colab T4 still best free option. Modal has best developer experience for paid serverless GPU. RunPod spot instances cheapest for burst. Kaggle broken for us. Lightning AI unexplored.
key_ecosystem_insights.inference_speed_2026: SGLang + LMDeploy lead at 16.2k tokens/sec on H100. TensorRT-LLM best throughput with 28min compilation. vLLM best flexibility. All irrelevant for our tree-based models.
